title: Practice extract: The 7:12
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 49 (Practice extract 'The 7:12' (teacher-written modern column, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 49: Language analysis in depth: choosing the best three quotations. Teacher-written for TGA. Read, then answer under time.

passage.title: The 7:12
paras: Every weekday I spend fifty minutes on the 7:12. Most people treat it as dead time: phones, headphones, eyes shut. I used to. Then, one grey March, the signal failed for an hour outside a village I had passed five hundred times and never seen. A woman across the aisle offered me half her orange. A student read us the funny bits of his textbook. By the time the train moved, the carriage was a small, temporary town. It has never happened again. But now I look up from my phone, just in case.

questions.q: Choose your three richest quotations for the question and give a reason for each
questions.a: For example: 'dead time' (wasted life); 'half her orange' (simple generosity); 'a small, temporary town' (community).

questions.q: Cut one thin quotation from this list and explain: 'grey March', 'fifty minutes', 'just in case'
questions.a: 'fifty minutes': a plain fact with little to analyse.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a 10-mark answer using exactly three quotations. Starter: 'The writer presents the delay as...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: 'dead time' (metaphor of waste); the precise, homely kindness of 'half her orange'; 'a small, temporary town'; the structural turn from routine to the delay to the reflective last line 'just in case'.

questions.q: Extend: self-mark with the ladder and note one gain
Stretch: add a sentence on the effect of the final phrase 'just in case'
questions.a: For example: it shows lasting hope: the writer now watches for connection.

questions.q: Which is the richest quotation for 'how the writer presents the delay as valuable'?
options: 'the carriage was a small, temporary town'
questions.a: A) 'the carriage was a small, temporary town'. The metaphor turns strangers into a community and suggests the moment's fragility.

questions.q: A rich quotation is one that...
questions.a: C) you can say two or more things about
options: you can say two or more things about

questions.q: Answer the ponder: why do three good quotations beat ten?
questions.a: Depth earns marks; listing does not.
